All the members present unanimously voted in favour of the proposal. After that, the committee chair called for a vote on approving the whole bill with the changes made by the committee. All the members present unanimously voted in favour.

meetings.title: 9th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: As the first item on today’s agenda, the committee decided on how to proceed the review of the Bill on amendment to Act No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act), proposed by the Government and sponsored by Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. In this regard, Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed proposed that the deadline for the Committee to complete its review of the Bill be set as 16 September 2026; that the public be invited to submit comments on the Bill from today until 10 August 2026; and that written comments on the Bill be sought from relevant institutions. The proposal was seconded by Hulhumalé Medhu Constituency Member Abdulla Shaheem. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present at the Committee meeting who participated in the vote. As the second item, the Committee continued its review of the Bill on amendment to Act No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act), proposed by the Government and sponsored by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. In this regard, Committee members deliberated on the comments submitted by the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority (MIRA) regarding the Bill. With regard to MIRA’s comment concerning the definition of “plastic bag” in Article 76 of the Bill, Maafannu Hulhangu Constituency Member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim proposed, and Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed seconded, amending Article 76 (ހލ) to read as follows: “‘Plastic bag’ means a bag made of plastic (including oxo-degradable plastic and degradable plastic made from synthetic polymers) that is used for carrying goods, excluding a bag in which goods are packaged to the extent necessarily required for their sale.” All the members present at the committee meeting voted in favour of the proposal. After that, the Committee continued reading the Bill on the record from Article 15 to its completion.

meetings.summary: On today’s agenda was to review pending cases before the committee. As the first item on the agenda, the committee discussed a case submitted to the committee concerning Fenaka Corporation in Fuvahmulah City. Following deliberations, Maafannu West Constituency member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, proposed to conclude the matter after obtaining the latest update in writing from Fenaka Corporation. The motion was seconded by Abdulla Shazeem, Member for Hulhumalé Central Constituency. The motion was approved unanimously by all the members present. As the second item, the members deliberated on a letter informing the activities of Auditor general’s office conducted in collaboration with the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions. The Committee decided to identify a date convenient for the Auditor General’s Office from 6, 7 or 8 July and to meet with the relevant officials of the Office to discuss the matters highlighted in the letter. As the third item, the committee reviewed a letter submitted by Project Thimaaveshi and several other associations expressing concerns regarding the potential damage that may result from reducing the protected areas of Eidigali Kilhi and Koattey for a proposed project to widen the Link Road in Hithadhoo, Addu City. Committee reviewed this together with another case regarding the same issue submitted by Galolhu North Constituency member Mohamed Ibrahim. Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, Member for Maafannu West Constituency, proposed to share the concerns raised in these two cases with the Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy and the Ministry of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development for their opinion. The motion was seconded by Ibrahim Naufal, Member for Mulaku Constituency. The voting details on the motion are provided in the “votes” section. Thereafter, the Committee reviewed a letter submitted by Galolhu North Constituency member Mohamed Ibrahim highlighting concerns regarding a proposed housing project in the Funavau area of Vilimalé. Committee members highlighted that in response to a question raised by a Member of the People’s Majlis, the Minister responsible for the relevant ministry had informed the People’s Majlis that a decision had been made to relocate the project to another area. Accordingly, the Committee decided not to proceed further with the matter. Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, Member for Maafannu West Constituency, proposed that a response be sent to MP Mohamed Ibrahim, referring to the information presented during the sitting of the People’s Majlis. The motion was seconded by Abdulla Shazeem, Member for Hulhumalé Central Constituency.

meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee discussed ongoing cases. As the first item, the committee discussed a case concerning a report submitted to the committee about the decision to ban plastic PET bottles below 500 ml. Once the floor was opened to the members for discussion, West Mafannu constituency member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim proposed meeting with the Ministry of Environment, the Business Council and the Ministry of Health to clarify the impact of this ban. He also proposed forming a subcommittee to review this matter. Both proposals were seconded by Mulaku constituency member Ibrahim Naufal. All the members present voted unanimously in favour of the proposals. After that, West Mafannu constituency member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim proposed that the subcommittee be mandated to review the case regarding the decision to ban plastic PET bottles below 500 ml and finalize the report. Then Mathiveri constituency member Hassan Zareer nominated the committee chairman South Mafannu constituency member Abdulla Rifau, Keyodhoo constituency member Mohamed Niushad and West Mafannu constituency member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim for the subcommittee. This proposal was seconded by Hithaadhoo constituency member Mohamed Siruhaan. All members present voted unanimously in favour of this proposal.
